papers.title: Sleep Homeostasis Has Circaseptan and Circatrigintan Cycles Over Year-Long Timescales.
papers.summary: Continuously recorded subscalp EEG in 20 healthy adults over 12-15 months and found that the nightly slope of slow-wave activity (0.5-4 Hz) was predominantly negative, confirming intact sleep homeostasis, and showed significant circaseptan (~7-day) and circatrigintan (~28-day) rhythms in most subjects. These results establish a normative baseline indicating sleep homeostatic regulation is organized across multiple timescales beyond a single night.

papers.title: NeuralFieldManifold: Uncovering the Manifold Geometry of Local Field Potentials
papers.summary: Analytically and empirically shows that lag-embedded local field potential dynamics lie on a low-dimensional K-torus, with each sustained oscillatory mode contributing an independent circular degree of freedom while aperiodic 1/f structure and noise add only geometric thickness. The authors introduce DeepLagField, a physics-informed network for nonstationary recordings, and report persistent homology signatures consistent with predicted toroidal Betti numbers in primate V1, rodent hippocampal, and mouse cortical EEG data, with decoding performance rivaling conventional spectral features.

papers.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
papers.summary: Presents the rationale and design of PD-CogT-Sleep, a monocentric, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial combining remotely delivered digital cognitive training with phase-targeted auditory stimulation to enhance deep sleep in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment (target N=50, 1:1 randomization). The primary outcome is executive function, with secondary and exploratory outcomes including other cognitive measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep EEG markers assessed at baseline, 5 weeks, and 3-month follow-up.

papers.title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Building Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Electroencephalography.
papers.summary: Reviews the translational evidence for AI-based clinical EEG analysis, arguing that high classification accuracy in research datasets does not establish clinical readiness and that translation should be judged by evidence strength rather than technical performance alone. The review examines target validity, data leakage, confounding, external validation, and clinically aligned metrics, and argues for clinical understandability and human-machine workflows over isolated classifiers.

papers.title: Clinical Validation of the New EEG Trend, Brain State of the Newborn, Against aEEG Interpretation.
papers.summary: Validated the automatically computed Brain State of the Newborn (BSN) EEG trend against expert visual aEEG interpretation in 731 epochs from 85 hypothermia-treated asphyxiated infants, finding BSN robustly differentiated aEEG background scores and correlated with recovery to continuous normal voltage (ρ=0.72). Concludes BSN offers a real-time automated complement to aEEG for assessing electrocortical recovery.

papers.title: Transient Alerting Effects of Karolinska Sleepiness Scale Ratings on Physiological and Driving Performance Indicators.
papers.summary: Pooled data from five driving simulator studies (83 participants) to test whether Karolinska Sleepiness Scale ratings induce a transient alerting effect, showing post-rating changes in blink duration, blink closing velocity, heart rate, parietal alpha power, and lane position variability lasting roughly 40 to over 120 s depending on indicator.

papers.title: Autonomic Reactivity and EEG-defined Clusters Reveal Distinct Chronic Pain Profiles.
papers.summary: In 177 patients with chronic pain after spine surgery, the authors integrated stress-related HRV LF/HF changes with resting-state EEG features via PCA and unsupervised clustering. A nominally significant HRV-group by EEG-cluster interaction was found, with the LF/HF-decrease group reporting higher pain scores within one EEG cluster, though main effects were not significant and findings require validation.

papers.title: Exchange of High-Frequency Medical Monitoring Data Using Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources for Interoperable Integration Into Clinical Practice and Research: Methodological Development Study.
papers.summary: Developed TIDE, an FHIR Release 4 package using a Metadata-Proxy pattern to standardize high-frequency medical monitoring data, with 7 primary FHIR artifacts and 16 component slices decoupling queryable clinical metadata from raw signal storage. Provides a modality-agnostic, standards-compliant framework demonstrated with EEG for interoperable clinical and research integration.

papers.title: ST-M2EDA: spatio-temporal metric-guided multi-stream expert domain adaptation network for fatigue monitoring.
papers.summary: Proposed ST-M2EDA, a spatio-temporal metric-guided multi-stream expert domain adaptation network combining SVD-based reconstruction, Mixup augmentation, DSBN with a ResNet-Transformer backbone, and MK-MMD for cross-subject EEG fatigue detection, achieving 90.54% average accuracy on the SEED-VIG dataset.

papers.title: Supporting the driver's perception cognition action loop using an embodied intelligent cockpit framework for explainable fatigue intervention.
papers.summary: In a simulator study with 40 licensed drivers, an explanatory speech warning based on multimodal fatigue detection and SHAP-based feature attribution was associated with a 0.192-s shorter mean braking reaction time and 0.085-m lower SDLP compared with generic speech after takeover in conditional automated driving.

papers.title: State-Dependent EEG Markers of Excitation/Inhibition and Hemodynamic State Are Associated with Random Noise Stimulation Effects.
papers.summary: Tested whether baseline and task-related EEG (aperiodic exponent) and fNIRS hemodynamic markers relate to transcranial random noise stimulation effects on mathematical learning, finding tRNS accelerated learning and that higher resting aperiodic exponent and lower resting HbO predicted greater stimulation gains, supporting a state-dependent framework.

papers.title: LaBraM at Scale: Scaling Data and Models for EEG Pretraining
papers.summary: Scaled the LaBraM EEG foundation model across 5.8M–1.97B parameters and 25,067–79,910 hours of EEG data, evaluating 23 tasks. The largest model (Atom-L*) reached 59.05% mean balanced accuracy in full fine-tuning, 3.61 points above the strongest baseline EEG foundation model, and found that stronger linear probing did not guarantee stronger full fine-tuning.

papers.title: GraTED: Graph--Tensor EEG Decoding for Passenger Hazard Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.summary: Proposed GraTED, a graph-tensor EEG decoding model that represents electrodes as a scalp-location graph and uses graph convolution plus low-rank tensor classification to preserve spatial and time-feature structure for passenger risk prediction and danger identification. It achieved the highest balanced accuracy across three evaluation settings on the 11-participant PassengerEEG dataset while using the fewest learnable parameters among seven baselines.

papers.title: Gotta Go Fast: Intended Concentric Effort Produces Divergent Myoelectric Spectral Profiles During Fatiguing, Load-Equated Resistance Exercise.
papers.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
papers.summary: Twenty recreationally active adults performed fatiguing unilateral leg extensions at 70% 1RM under maximal intended concentric velocity (Vmax) and 50%Vmax, with wavelet-based sEMG analysis showing Vmax suppressed high-frequency bands while 50%Vmax increased power across the spectrum; profiles converged asymmetrically at task failure (rho_c=0.98 overall).

papers.title: Mapping brain networks underlying abstract perceptual decision formation and its EEG signatures
papers.summary: Combining fMRI and EEG in a supramodal change-detection paradigm with individualized finite element head modeling, the study identified a decision-related network including parietal-opercular regions as dominant contributors to the centroparietal positivity (CPP) during abstract perceptual decisions.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during naturalistic smartphone interactions
papers.summary: Presents a publicly released multimodal BIDS-formatted dataset (OpenNeuro ds007537) of synchronized 64-channel EEG, eye-tracking, PPG, and GSR from 23 participants during 10 minutes of naturalistic smartphone use followed by a 5-minute nature-video relaxation condition, with TTL-triggered alignment and smartphone-use questionnaires.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of extending outpatient EEG to record sleep - A retrospective study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: In 1762 outpatient EEGs extended to ~40-50 min, N2 sleep was achieved in 70.5% of patients without sleep deprivation, and sleep recording detected unique interictal epileptiform discharges in an additional 12% beyond wakefulness (total yield OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.02-1.68), with the greatest incremental gain between 20 and 30 min.

papers.title: A phase-calibrated combined electrical-sensory neuromodulation platform for short-Term frontoparietal network modulation and cognitive fatigue resistance.
papers.summary: Developed a phase-calibrated multimodal neuromodulation platform combining tACS with visual and auditory rhythmic input, using individualized ERP-latency delay compensation, and tested it in a randomized sham-controlled crossover study with 15 participants. Phase-coordinated stimulation increased resting-state frontoparietal theta power and connectivity (wPLI) and reduced fatigue-related parietal alpha accumulation, with parietal alpha stability moderately associated with behavioral performance (r=0.577).

papers.title: Repeated prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation improves behavioral regulation and modulates resting-state EEG microstate dynamics in young adults with problematic smartphone use: a randomized sham-controlled longitudinal study.
papers.summary: Randomized 80 young adults with problematic smartphone use to active or sham left-DLPFC tDCS (2.0 mA, 12 weeks) and examined behavioral and resting-state EEG microstate outcomes. Active tDCS reduced objectively measured smartphone use, craving, and functional impairment and selectively altered microstate dynamics (e.g., decreased microstate C and increased D eyes-closed), without changes in global explained variance.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture alleviates TNBS-induced visceral pain and modulates cortical EEG rhythms in association with TREM1/DAP12 pathway inhibition: Enhanced effects with pharmacological TREM1 blockade.
papers.summary: In TNBS-induced visceral pain rats, electroacupuncture alleviated hyperalgesia and normalized cortical delta/theta EEG dysrhythmia in association with suppression of microglial TREM1/DAP12 neuroinflammation; pharmacological TREM1 blockade mimicked and enhanced these effects.

papers.title: Intraoperative electroencephalography burst suppression during endoscopic third ventriculostomy: Case report and implications for neuromonitoring.
papers.summary: Reported a case of a 28-year-old woman undergoing endoscopic third ventriculostomy who developed intraoperative hemodynamic crises coinciding with bilateral EEG burst suppression, which resolved slower than hemodynamics. Suggests processed intraoperative EEG may serve as an early sign of acute cerebral disturbance, though its added value remains unproven.

papers.title: Targeted gene therapy alleviates epilepsy and hyperexcitability in models of SCN2A deficiency.
papers.summary: Using a gene-trap Scn2a-deficient mouse model on a seizure-prone background and human cortical organoids with a SCN2A-truncating variant, AAV-mediated KCNA1 expression normalized elevated neuronal firing and reduced spontaneous seizure burden, providing proof of principle for drug-controllable KCNA1 gene therapy in SCN2A loss-of-function epilepsy.

papers.title: Neural and behavioral signatures of live and video demonstrations in bimanual interpersonal coordination: An EEG and kinematic study.
papers.summary: Investigated how live versus video modeling affects neural oscillations (mu and high-beta) and kinematic coordination during a bimanual interpersonal coordination task in 20 right-handed females. Live-model interaction produced stronger high-beta suppression and more stable kinematic coupling, and mu suppression during observation increased across practice phases.

papers.title: Neural correlates of perceptual biases in duration perception.
papers.summary: In a duration reproduction task with EEG, frontocentral CNV depended on the previous stimulus duration regardless of sequential dependence, whereas right parietal slow potentials and P2 amplitude were associated with inter-individual differences in sequential dependence and central tendency, and a Bayesian model reproduced the observed CNV dynamics.

papers.title: Unexplained neurological deterioration after acute brain injury: A structured intensive care framework for targeted continuous electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: Presented a narrative review and structured intensive care framework for evaluating unexplained neurological deterioration after acute brain injury, defining when targeted continuous EEG is most informative. Emphasizes that cEEG should complement, not replace, clinical examination, neuroimaging, and correction of systemic physiology.

papers.title: Thought-deciphering via hierarchical EEG-to-text alignment
papers.summary: Proposed a hierarchical alignment framework for sentence-level EEG-to-text classification, aiming to retrieve a read sentence using its context and EEG as inputs. Aims to advance non-invasive brain-to-text BCIs and clarify how EEG relates to text at letter, word, sentence, and semantic levels.

papers.title: In-person UCLA-PEERS® program for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder in Italy: study protocol for a pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial with pragmatic features and exploratory EEG markers of treatment response.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a two-arm pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing in-person Italian UCLA-PEERS® against treatment as usual in 36 adolescents with level 1 autism spectrum disorder, with feasibility measures as the primary focus and the QSQ-R social functioning measure as prespecified principal clinical outcome. It also plans to derive baseline N400 congruency effects from EEG during a gesture-word integration task to explore associations with treatment response.

papers.title: Reducing the Risk of Gradient Induced EEG Hardware Heating During Simultaneous EEG-fMRI
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that placing EEG amplifiers and powerpacks within the MRI bore during simultaneous EEG-fMRI creates significant gradient-induced heating risk at 3T and 7T, which can be mitigated by reducing gradient slew rate (e.g., to 61 T/m/s at 7T) or increasing the distance between hardware and magnet isocentre by 30 cm.

papers.title: Multimodal characterization of putative pan-inhibitory viral constructs in macaque monkeys
papers.summary: The authors characterized three Dlx5-6-derived pan-inhibitory viral constructs in seven rhesus macaques using in vivo electrophysiology, in vitro slice electrophysiology, and immunohistochemistry, finding transgene expression restricted to inhibitory neurons in 81-97% of cells but only 32-64% of local GABAergic neurons, with uneven subtype coverage (strong in parvalbumin-positive, sparse in calbindin-positive, minimal in calretinin-positive interneurons). A DLX2.0-ChrimsonR construct supported effective in vivo optotagging, whereas h56D-bReaChES most effectively suppressed neural activity.

papers.title: Norepinephrine inhibits Afferent activation of NTS Catecholamine Neurons in Mice
papers.summary: Using patch-clamp electrophysiology in mouse horizontal brainstem slices, this study shows that norepinephrine inhibits solitary tract-evoked EPSCs onto NTS tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons in a concentration-dependent, alpha-adrenergic receptor-mediated manner, largely through a presynaptic mechanism. NPY similarly reduced ST-EPSC amplitude via Y2 receptors, and NE plus NPY produced additive or synergistic inhibition, implicating noradrenergic-peptidergic interaction in visceral sensory processing.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted chemometric analysis of salivary ATR-FTIR spectra for the diagnosis of oral submucous fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study analyzed salivary ATR-FTIR spectra from 450 participants (150 oral submucous fibrosis, 150 with adverse oral habits, 150 controls) using PCA and machine learning classifiers with stratified 10-fold cross-validation, where XGBoost achieved accuracies of 90.62% for Normal versus Habit, 97.67% for Normal versus OSMF, and 91.30% for three-class classification. In an independent 90-participant validation cohort, accuracy was 80.0% for OSMF versus Normal and 71.7% for Habit versus Normal.

papers.title: Case Report: Successful treatment of drug-resistant epilepsy with unilateral deep brain stimulation of the anterior nucleus of the thalamus.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 29-year-old woman with drug-resistant epilepsy after childhood treatment of a suprasellar germ cell tumor who underwent unilateral right anterior nucleus of the thalamus deep brain stimulation because of a right-predominant epileptogenic network and anatomical constraints preventing left electrode placement. Seizure frequency fell from about 10 per day to one per day after stimulation initiation, with a sustained approximately 60% reduction and no adverse events at 9-month follow-up.

papers.title: An integrative view of human nociceptor diversity: from microneurography to molecular identity.
papers.summary: This review integrates microneurography-defined biophysical hallmarks of human nociceptors (e.g., activity-dependent slowing, recovery cycle signatures, following frequency) with patch-clamp, Patch-seq, transcriptomic atlases, and computational modeling to link nerve fiber function to molecular identity and ion channel mechanisms in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Calcified choroid plexus papilloma of the temporal horn presenting with seizures in an adult without hydrocephalus: An illustrative case.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 50-year-old woman with focal impaired awareness seizures found to have a calcified mesial temporal lesion without hydrocephalus, which imaging suggested was a cavernoma but surgical pathology confirmed as a choroid plexus papilloma. After levetiracetam treatment and tumor resection, she had no postoperative seizures and no neurological deficits.

papers.title: A multimodal optimisation framework for cardiac electrophysiology model personalisation using computed tomography and 12-lead electrocardiogram: Algorithm development and validation.
papers.summary: A multimodal optimization framework combining CT and 12-lead ECG for personalizing cardiac electrophysiology models was tested in six patients, achieving 91.20% mean QRS peak accuracy and reducing average QRS duration error to 3.94 ms (vs. 37.42 ms baseline), with simulations reproducing clinical VT patterns in four patients.

papers.title: Atypical Pediatric Epilepsy: A Narrative Review of Classification, Diagnosis, and Emerging Therapeutics.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes classification, epidemiology, etiology, and emerging precision therapies for atypical pediatric epilepsies, including Lennox-Gastaut, Dravet, infantile epileptic spasms, and FIRES. It emphasizes the diagnostic gap from phenotypic overlap, EEG limitations, and barriers to timely genetic testing, and highlights a shift toward targeted pharmacologic, antisense oligonucleotide, gene therapy, and neuromodulation approaches.

papers.title: Restitution properties during ventricular fibrillation and the effects of cardiac pacing location on ventricular electrophysiology in the rabbit heart.
papers.summary: Using Langendorff-perfused rabbit hearts and monophasic action potential recordings from left ventricular apex and base, this study tested whether pacing site and prior activation history affect ventricular repolarization. Steady-state APD, effective refractory period, and conduction time restitution were largely independent of pacing location, whereas during early ventricular fibrillation APD showed short-term cardiac memory dependent on preceding diastolic interval and APD for about the first 30 beats before these relationships deteriorated.

papers.title: Study on methods for deriving spatial distribution of electron temperature and density from RGB (red-green-blue) digital image in non-thermal equilibrium plasma.
papers.summary: A method was developed to derive spatial distributions of electron temperature and density in non-thermal equilibrium plasma from calibrated RGB JPEG images by relating relative RGB values to excitation temperature and average grayscale to density, validated using blackbody radiation and line-pair methods.

papers.title: Design and Validation of Multiplexed Respiratory RT-LAMP assay for the differentiation of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in COVID-19 Pandemic Samples from Western Kenya.
papers.summary: This study designed and validated a multiplexed RT-LAMP assay with fluorescently labelled LAMP probes for simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and RSV, evaluated on mid-nasal swabs from 175 MALCOV cohort participants in Kisumu, Kenya against an RT-PCR reference test. Compared with RT-PCR at 40 minutes, RT-LAMP sensitivity was 82.64% (95% CI 74.70-88.92%) and specificity 100% (95% CI 93.40-100%), with a mean time to positive result of 11 minutes.

papers.title: Atypical Atrial Flutter From Lipomatous Hypertrophy of the Interatrial Septum in a Procedure-Naive Patient.
keywords: lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum
papers.summary: This case report describes an 86-year-old procedure-naive man with new-onset atypical atrial flutter at 280 beats/min in whom intracardiac echocardiography identified lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum and electroanatomic mapping localized earliest focal activation to the superior posteroseptal right atrium at the LHIS site. Radiofrequency ablation terminated the flutter and rendered it noninducible, supporting LHIS as an isolated arrhythmogenic substrate.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
